requirements.statement: The commodity page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'About the consignment' above the heading 'What are you importing?', the Draft tag and notification reference above the caption, and a search field labelled 'Search for a commodity'.

requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p8-003, -p8-004, -p8-005, -p8-006 and -p8-008 show the same title, caption, heading, Draft strip and label today.

requirements.statement: The commodity page's inset text reads 'You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the one-notification-per-certificate rule in terms of the ITAHC, the certificate traders know.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the inset reads 'A separate notification is required for each health certificate. Consignments that do not require a health certificate must still be notified.' (trace-animals-fit-p8-007).

requirements.statement: On a live-animals notification the commodity search hint reads 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).', with no 'Enter at least 3 characters.' sentence.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording wins by default; DR1 left the hint wording unruled, and the reason the frontend departed from it (no common names in the data) no longer holds, since 'cattle' now finds cattle species.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'You can search by commodity name (for example, Cow), commodity code (0102), or species name (Bos taurus). Enter at least 3 characters.' (trace-animals-fit-p8-009); the Welsh mirrors it.

requirements.statement: A closed 'Help with commodity codes' details component below the search explains 'Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.' and 'A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.', and links to the Trade Tariff tool at https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff in a new tab.
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their commodity code need a way to look it up.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p8-012 to -p8-016 show the same details summary, both paragraphs and the new-tab Trade Tariff link today.

requirements.statement: In the commodity code help, '(opens in a new tab)' sits on its own line after the 'Trade Tariff tool' link, as Design Release 2.1 lays it out, and stays part of the link's accessible text.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 breaks the line before '(opens in a new tab)'; keeping the words inside the link keeps the link purpose announced, as the page's accessibility check requires.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the link text 'Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)' runs on one line with the sentence (trace-animals-fit-p8-015).

conflicts.about: Apparent data errors in DR2.1's species list: 'Equus cabalus' and 'Eq cabalus*asinus' for Equus caballus, and the near-duplicate 'Other mammalia' / 'Other Mammalia'.

positions.says: Horse species are 'Eq cabalus*asinus', 'Equus asinus' and 'Equus cabalus'.
Other live mammals holds both 'Other mammalia' and 'Other Mammalia', each 'Other mammal'.
The horse species renders 'Equus cabalus' though its id is equus-caballus, so the name looks misspelt.
The real service names the horse species 'Equus caballus'.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype default.

conflicts.outcome: Correct DR2.1's species data rather than copy it: the horse species reads 'Equus caballus' and the mule 'Eq caballus*asinus', and Other live mammals holds a single 'Other Mammalia' (Other mammal) entry. The species display text is what the backend sends downstream as the GBN-AG scientificName, with no species code beside it, so a misspelt Latin name would reach the receiving service as a wrong scientific name, and two entries that differ only in a capital letter would reach it as the same species. The prototype's own id (horse-equus-caballus) already spells the name correctly. Every other species name, common name and code is exactly as DR2.1 gives it.
